From town centre to river

Event Planners in Hornsby

Hornsby Shire runs from a suburban town centre to acreage at Galston and the Hawkesbury at Brooklyn, and the planning problem is different at each end. Tell us where your event actually sits and we will pass the brief to planners who cover that part of the shire.

  • Two rail lines meetThe North Shore and Northern lines join at Hornsby station.

Half an hour north of the station, the rules change completely.

Water for the caterer, power for the lights, a road a coach can turn on, and a fire ban that can arrive the week of your event. None of that applies in Waitara.

Hornsby Shire is often called the bushland shire, and the name is doing real work. Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park takes up a large share of it, the northern end is acreage and orchard country around Arcadia, Galston and Glenorie, and the shire keeps going until it hits the Hawkesbury at Brooklyn. People looking for event planners in Hornsby are usually planning one of two quite different events, and the first useful question is which one.

The first is a straightforward suburban function within a few minutes of the town centre, where two rail lines meet and guests can get themselves home. The second is on private land in the upper shire or down on the river, where you are effectively building a venue for a day. Both are common. They need different planners, different budgets and, in bushfire season, different contingency plans.

In and around Hornsby

What are you planning in Hornsby?

What you can do here depends almost entirely on the address. The same brief costs and behaves differently in Waitara than it does on ten acres at Arcadia.

Start with

Weddings

Acreage in the upper shire is the draw, and the bush setting is genuinely beautiful, but a property wedding is a build. Water, power, bathrooms, a wet weather structure and a road a coach can use all have to be confirmed before you set a date.

Find planners

Parties and milestones

Backyard sixtieths and twenty firsts around Pennant Hills, Beecroft and Cherrybrook are steady work, and the constraint is usually noise and parking on narrow streets rather than space. Further north the constraint flips: plenty of room, no services, and a long drive for every supplier.

Find planners

Corporate events

Most corporate work here is small and local: team days, client functions and end of year nights for businesses along the rail corridor. Groups that want a bush setting for a strategy day tend to look at the acreage properties, which brings catering and transport back into the budget.

Find planners

Engagement parties

These often happen at a family home, which in the upper shire can mean a large garden and a marquee. Check the driveway before anything else. A truck that cannot turn around at the top of a rural drive becomes your problem on the morning of the event.

Find planners

Proposals

The lookouts and waterways in and around Ku-ring-gai Chase are the obvious setting, and the practical issues are access and light. Park gates close, tracks can be shut in fire season, and if you are heading to Brooklyn or Dangar Island you are working to a boat timetable.

Find planners

Private celebrations

Christenings, anniversaries and wakes usually stay close to the town centre for a reason: guests can reach Hornsby by train from both the North Shore and the Northern line. If the family property is at Glenorie or Wisemans Ferry, budget for transport rather than assuming people will drive themselves.

Planning support

How much help do you want in Hornsby?

A town centre function with a venue that owns the kitchen and the bar can often run on coordination alone. A property event in the upper shire is closer to full planning, because there is no venue absorbing the risk.

Full planning

A planner carries the whole build with you, from the first budget conversation to the last supplier leaving.

Usually engaged nine to fourteen months out.

You have made a start. A planner picks up the parts that have stalled and brings the rest into one plan.

Your plan is built. A coordinator takes it over in the final weeks and runs the day so you can be in it.

Usually engaged four to eight weeks out.

Venue sourcing

Planners who know a market can shortlist against your date, your numbers and your budget rather than sending you back to the same search results.

Event coordination

Coordination is the execution layer: suppliers confirmed, a run sheet everyone has, and one person answering questions on the day.

Wedding coordination

A wedding coordinator takes a plan you have already built and runs the day itself, so nobody in the wedding party is directing traffic.

Choosing well

Finding the right planner in Hornsby

The questions that matter most in this shire are about the site rather than the styling. Work through these before anyone starts talking about colour palettes, table settings or a mood board.

No. 01

Ask what they have run without mains services

A property event needs water, power and waste solved before anything else. Ask a planner how many generator run events they have delivered, what size unit they specified, and how they handled bathrooms for the guest number. Someone who answers in specifics has done it. Someone who says it will be fine has not.

No. 02

Get the fire season plan in writing

Total fire bans are declared at short notice and can rule out open flame, fire pits, fireworks and sparklers on the day. If any of those are in your plan, ask what the alternative is and who makes the call. A November or December date in the upper shire makes this a live question, not a formality.

No. 03

Check whether suppliers charge to come north

Thornleigh is a short run from most of northern Sydney. Glenorie, Wisemans Ferry and the river settlements are not. Ask a planner which suppliers they can bring that far without a travel loading, and whether the quote you are reading already includes it. Delivery and collection are two trips, not one.

No. 04

Talk about the cold before you talk about the view

Winter nights in the upper shire sit noticeably below the coast, and a marquee without heating empties by nine. Ask what heating is specified, how it is powered, and whether the sides can be closed. The same question applies to an evening in April, when the temperature drops faster than people expect.

In the upper shire you are not booking a venue. You are building one for a day.

On the ground

Two shires in one: suburb and bush

Hornsby Shire covers so much ground that a single set of local advice would be useless. These three things separate the southern end from everything north and west of it.

Distance is the first budget line

From Hornsby town centre to Glenorie or Wisemans Ferry is another 30 to 50 minutes of driving, and every supplier makes that trip twice. Caterers, hire companies, sound and lighting all price it. It also changes your guests' behaviour: people who would take a train to Waitara will drive to Arcadia, which means car parking on a rural property and a serious think about how anyone gets home. Coaches are the usual answer, and they need somewhere to turn around.

The river is its own logistics problem

Brooklyn, Dangar Island and the Hawkesbury settlements are genuinely lovely and genuinely difficult. Dangar Island has no road access at all, so guests, food, furniture, ice and staff arrive by boat on a timetable someone has to own. That means a departure time, a manifest, a plan for latecomers and a last service back. Weather on the river can move a departure. If you are considering a Hawkesbury event, ask a planner whether they have run one, not whether they would like to.

Bushfire season sits inside the plan, not beside it

From roughly October to March, a total fire ban can be declared days out and it removes open flame from your run sheet without negotiation. On acreage the risk goes further than candles: access roads can close, and smoke can make an outdoor space unusable even when nothing local is burning. Build the alternative before you need it.

  • Nominate an indoor or covered fallback for the ceremony
  • Replace candles, fire pits and sparklers with lighting that does not need a flame
  • Agree who monitors conditions in the final week and who decides
  • Keep a second contact for every supplier in case a road closes

Questions

Planning an event in Hornsby

What does an event planner charge in Hornsby Shire?

Fees track scope and site difficulty rather than the suburb name. A coordinated function at a venue near the station is a defined piece of work with a known finish. A property event at Galston or Arcadia adds site visits, generator and bathroom specification, transport and a contingency plan, and the fee reflects those hours. Ask for the quote against your actual address, because the same guest number can cost very differently 40 minutes apart.

Can we hold a wedding on acreage at Galston or Arcadia?

Yes, and it is one of the main reasons people plan events in this shire, but a paddock is not a venue. You are supplying water, power, lighting, bathrooms, a wet weather structure, waste removal and a road that a coach and a delivery truck can both use. Check whether the property has any council conditions on functions. Then check the month against fire season, because a December date carries a risk a May date does not.

How do guests get to an event on the Hawkesbury?

By boat for the island settlements and by car or train to Brooklyn for everything else, which means the transport plan is part of the event rather than an afterthought. Dangar Island has no road access, so you are scheduling departures, counting people on and off, and setting a last service back. Build in a buffer for weather. A river crossing that is delayed 20 minutes moves your entire run sheet.

Does a fire ban actually stop an event?

It stops the parts of it that involve flame, and on rural land it can do more than that. A total fire ban rules out fire pits, fireworks, sparklers and in some cases open cooking, and it can be declared with a day or two of warning between October and March. Access roads may also close during an active fire. Ask your planner to write the alternative into the plan when you book, not when the ban is declared.

Is winter workable for an outdoor event up here?

It is, with heating specified properly and an honest conversation about the temperature. The upper shire runs colder than the coast, and a clear night in June or July drops away quickly once the sun goes. Marquee heating needs power, so on a property that usually means generator capacity you have already sized for lighting and catering. Guests also leave earlier when they are cold, so plan speeches and cake before the chill arrives.

Do we need a permit for a ceremony in a national park?

Usually yes. Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park covers a large part of the shire and organised ceremonies in national parks generally require a booking or permit from the park authority, with conditions on numbers, vehicles, chairs and amplified sound. Apply early for spring and autumn weekends. A planner can lodge and track the application, but the approval is not theirs to give, so never confirm a date with guests before it is granted.
